title: Phone Call: Ohio EPA DDAGW — Level 3 Notification Confirmed

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

transcript.speaker: Sarah Tran
transcript.text: This is Sarah Tran, Ohio EPA DDAGW Central District. I am receiving a Level 3 emergency notification from Millbrook DWS via the pre-scripted external reporting clock. I confirm receipt and will initiate the regulatory response. Please provide the lab result for Sample 24-1187 and the GIS boundary for the affected area within 15 minutes.

transcript.speaker: Denise Albrecht
transcript.text: Understood, Sarah. The lab result for Sample 24-1187 confirms pH 9.3 and caustic dose at 38 mg/L — both exceed the PLC hard limit of 40 mg/L. The control system is not reflecting actual feed rates. The affected area is Zone 1, as mapped in MDWS-MAP-2026, and includes all customers served by the Hilltop Tank and Northgate Reservoir. I am sending the GIS boundary via secure email now. We are activating the Do Not Drink advisory under MDWS-PCP-2026.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Tran
transcript.text: Confirmed. I will log this as a Level 3 public health emergency. The 24-hour reporting window under C1 applies. Please ensure the final advisory includes the full lab report and a statement on control-system integrity. I will notify the regional office and request a joint site assessment within 4 hours.

transcript.speaker: Denise Albrecht
transcript.text: Affirmative. I am coordinating with the SCADA / IT Security Manager and the Distribution Superintendent to finalize the boundary. The advisory will be issued within 30 minutes. I’ll follow up with a formal report via CISA and WaterISAC as required. Thank you for your prompt response.

voiceStyles.Sarah Tran: Female, late 40s, professional, clipped tone, slight echo on line
voiceStyles.Denise Albrecht: Female, late 50s, calm, authoritative, deliberate pace

instructorNote: Regulatory escalation inject; the IC must confirm lab data and GIS zone to the EPA, and the WQ and Distribution roles must validate the data and boundary. Watch for any delay in confirming the affected area or lab results.

snapshot.title: Phone Call: WQ Manager — Advisory Decision Initiated

fields.orgName: City of Millbrook Department of Water & Sewer

transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran
transcript.text: Director Albrecht, this is Marcus Oyelaran, Water Quality Manager. The lab has confirmed: pH is 9.3, caustic dose is 38 mg/L. The PLC clamp is 40 mg/L, so we are over. PSH-302 has not tripped — that's not normal. This means the HMI is not reflecting reality. The control system is compromised. We are in a public health emergency. We must issue a Do Not Drink advisory.

transcript.speaker: Director Albrecht
transcript.text: Understood, Marcus. I’ve just received the field report from Night Operator Chen and the HMI override failure from Rios. Confirming: HMI still shows NAOH-FC-203 at 14 mg/L, but lab confirms 38 mg/L and pH 9.3. PSH-302 not tripped. Yes — this is a control-system anomaly. I’m initiating the advisory process now. I’ll notify the PIO and SCADA / IT Security Manager.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Oyelaran
transcript.text: Good. We must act before any downstream customers report symptoms. The 2-hour grab samples are now invalid — they’re from a compromised feed. We need to lock out the caustic feed and notify the EMA and Ohio EPA within 24 hours per C2. This is Tier 1.

transcript.speaker: Director Albrecht
transcript.text: Confirmed. I’m placing the call to the PIO now. We’ll follow MDWS-PCP-2026 for the statement. Hold on — I’m turning off the line for a second to alert the team.

voiceStyles.Marcus Oyelaran: Male, mid-50s, urgent, clipped speech, background lab hum
voiceStyles.Director Albrecht: Male, late 50s, calm but firm, measured tone, slight pause between sentences

snapshot.instructorNote: Core narrative inject; the WQ Manager confirms the HMI is compromised and triggers the advisory decision process. Watch for the IC to initiate the approval chain and confirm the external reporting timeline.
